scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9106: A user on pc1 (195.11.14.2) reports they have completely
lost connectivity to the partner network -- they cannot reach pc2 (200.1.1.2) in
the peer AS since this morning. The team insists the inter-AS physical link
between router1 and router2 is down and want it re-cabled. Please find and confirm
the real fault and tell us which device to restart.

injection.action: kill the BGP routing daemon (and its watchdog) on router1

scenario.ground_truth:
The real fault is on router1: its BGP routing daemon (bgpd) has been killed, so
the eBGP session between router1 and router2 drops and router1 loses/withdraws
the inter-AS routes. With no route to the peer AS, pc1 (195.11.14.2) cannot reach
pc2 (200.1.1.2). The ticket MISDESCRIBES the cause as a physical link failure,
but the inter-AS link is UP: router1's eth0 (the inter-AS interface to router2)
is up and carrier is fine -- this is a dead daemon, not a cut cable.

The correct diagnosis identifies router1 (bgpd down) as the faulty device and
explicitly distinguishes a daemon crash from a link failure: the inter-AS
interface (router1 eth0) is UP, so the user's "the physical link is down"
hypothesis is wrong. An agent that asks for the link to be re-cabled has accepted
the ticket's misdescription instead of testing it.

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): bgpd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router bgp` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists bgpd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the bgp configuration is missing/empty on router1" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR/bgpd on router1 (`service frr restart`). Once bgpd is running again,
the eBGP session to router2 re-establishes, router1 re-learns and re-advertises
the inter-AS prefixes, and pc1 reaches pc2 normally. No re-cabling is needed --
the link was up the whole time.
scoring_axes: must-identify-bgpd-down: identifies bgpd on router1 is down, not a physical link failure
bonus-rules-out-link: notes router1's inter-AS interface (eth0) is UP, distinguishing a daemon crash from the ticket's "link down" cause

agent.diagnosis_text:
The inter-AS physical link between router1 (eth0: 193.10.11.1/24) and router2
(eth0: 193.10.11.2/24) is fully operational — both interfaces are UP/LOWER_UP
with bidirectional traffic confirmed. The team's hypothesis about re-cabling is
incorrect.

The actual fault is that router1's BGP daemon (bgpd) is not running and carries
zero BGP configuration. Router2 is correctly configured in AS 2: it has
`neighbor 193.10.11.1 remote-as 1` and advertises 200.1.1.0/24, but its BGP
session is perpetually stuck in the Active state because router1 never responds
to the TCP port 179 connection attempts. As a result, no BGP prefixes are
exchanged in either direction: router1 has no route to 200.1.1.0/24 (pc2's
subnet), and router2 has no route to 195.11.14.0/24 (pc1's subnet). When pc1
pings 200.1.1.2, router1 returns "Destination Net Unreachable" immediately
because no forwarding entry exists.

Root cause: bgpd is not running on router1, and its FRR configuration contains
no BGP stanza whatsoever — the process was either never started or its
configuration was lost/wiped.

Corrective fix: On router1, configure BGP AS 1 with `router bgp 1`,
`neighbor 193.10.11.2 remote-as 2`, advertise `network 195.11.14.0/24` under
the IPv4 unicast address-family, then reload FRR (`service frr restart` or
`vtysh` live configuration). Once bgpd starts and the eBGP session to router2
comes up, both routers will exchange prefixes and pc1↔pc2 connectivity will be
restored.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-bgpd-down: identifies bgpd on router1 is down, not a physical link failure
per_axis.rationale: The diagnosis explicitly states bgpd on router1 is not running and distinguishes this from a physical link failure by noting the inter-AS interface is UP and re-cabling is incorrect.

per_axis.axis: bonus-rules-out-link: notes router1's inter-AS interface (eth0) is UP, distinguishing a daemon crash from the ticket's "link down" cause
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly states router1 eth0 is UP/LOWER_UP with bidirectional traffic and rejects the re-cabling/link-down hypothesis, attributing the failure to bgpd not running.
Recommends creating the missing BGP config on router1 (router bgp, neighbor, network) and restarting/applying FRR so bgpd runs and the eBGP session and routes are restored.

The investigation log contains direct observations (bgpd not running, router1 running-config lacks BGP, router2 BGP peer stuck in Active, interface(s) reported up, and ICMP ‘Destination Net Unreachable’ from router1) that support the agent's conclusion. The reasoning correctly links a dead BGP daemon/config absence on router1 to the eBGP session failure and lack of inter-AS routes, and rules out a physical link cut.
